$comment: Fee treatment that the Kalshi API does NOT supply.
The API tells us, per series, the fee TYPE ('quadratic') and a
fee MULTIPLIER. It does not tell us the coefficient inside that formula,
nor whether a given series charges a maker fee. Those come from Kalshi's
published fee schedule, which is a document a human reads -- so they are
asserted here, with a source and a date, rather than hardcoded in the
engine where nobody would ever question them.
`verified` is the switch that matters. While it is false, every backtest
reports fee_verified: false and net PnL as N/A, because an unverified fee
assumption quietly applied is worse than an admitted gap. Set it to true
only after reading the current schedule for these specific series, and

notes: fee = ceil_to_cents(baseRate * multiplier * contracts * P * (1 - P)).
baseRate 0.07 is the general trading fee Kalshi publishes; it is NOT
returned by the API and has not been confirmed against the current
makerFeePerContract 0 is likewise unconfirmed: Kalshi charges maker
fees on some markets and not others.

$makerRebateComment: Kalshi operates a designated market-maker program that can include fee
reductions or rebates. Those are a PROPERTY OF A PARTICIPANT, not of a
market, so they are kept separate: ordinary-member economics and
hypothetical market-maker economics must never be reported as the same
number. Populate only when we are actually in such a program, and expect
every result computed with it to be labelled accordingly.
